Voltage is the electrical "pressure" that pushes electricity through a circuit, measured in volts.

Think of it like water pressure in a pipe. Higher pressure (voltage) pushes more water (current) through.

FTC robots use 12V batteries (nominal), though a fully charged battery reads around 13-14V at rest.

Current is the rate of electrical flow, measured in amps.

Different components draw different amounts: a small sensor might draw milliamps, while a motor under load can draw several amps.

When motors work hard, like pushing against a wall or climbing, they draw more current. This increased demand has a side effect called voltage sag.

When motors draw lots of current, the battery voltage drops temporarily. This is called voltage sag.

A battery reading 13V at rest may sag to 11.5V under heavy motor load. This is normal. The voltage recovers when the load decreases.

However, if it sags too low, the robot can brownout and reset.

Voltage ranges to know:

11V or below means the battery is too low. Charge or replace it before a match.

12-13V is acceptable but not ideal.

13V and above is good, showing a healthy, well-charged battery.

Always monitor voltage during matches to avoid brownouts, which cause the robot to lose power and reset mid-match.
